categories.intent: Whether login credentials are stored using a modern, sufficiently slow, salted hashing algorithm rather than a fast general-purpose hash.

categories.fixtureRequirement: A fixture handler that hashes a password-named value with a fast/unsalted primitive must trigger the rule; a paired fixture using a slow salted KDF (bcrypt/argon2/scrypt) must not.
categories.evidenceRequirement: detector-evidenced (decisionMode: evidence, cleanClaim: never-without-denominator per registry/rules/security/crypto-data-privacy.json); produces an UNADJUDICATED candidate requiring independent adjudication before any verdict.

categories.intent: Whether session cookies are issued with the browser protections (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite) needed to resist theft and cross-site misuse.

categories.intent: Password-strength policy, account-lockout thresholds, multi-factor enforcement, username/email enumeration resistance, constant-time credential comparison, remember-me hardening, and bot/automation protection on authentication forms.
categories.relationshipToSource: Restates the security concern raised under the listed creator.security ledger area(s) as an original classification decision; does not reproduce any ledger item's title or notes text.

exclusion.reason: These are policy-threshold and product-feature decisions (what complexity to require, whether to add MFA, how to throttle enumeration, whether to add a CAPTCHA) rather than a fixed code pattern; a static detector cannot tell an acceptable threshold from an unacceptable one without organization-specific policy input, and constant-time comparison requires semantic data-flow reasoning beyond a pattern match. Recorded as an architecture/policy backlog item, not smuggled into an existing rule's ownership.

categories.evidenceRequirement: policy-input-required: no static pattern can serve as sufficient evidence; any suggestion here must terminate in a human/product-owner decision, never a model verdict.

categories.intent: Session idle/absolute timeout duration, full session invalidation on logout, JWT claim-by-claim validation and algorithm-confusion resistance, short-lived access-token issuance, refresh-token rotation, and token-revocation mechanisms.
categories.relationshipToSource: Restates the security concern raised under the listed creator.security ledger area(s) as an original classification decision; does not reproduce any ledger item's title or notes text.

exclusion.reason: Timeout durations and rotation cadence are policy choices with no universal correct value; full-invalidation-on-logout and revocation-mechanism existence require runtime/integration verification rather than a source-level pattern; JWT algorithm-confusion resistance requires verifying the specific verification-call configuration, which the tokens category's auth.jwt-without-verification rule already partially covers for the narrower no-verification-at-all case. The broader claim-level and lifecycle items remain an architecture backlog rather than being folded into the tokens category's ownership.

categories.evidenceRequirement: policy-input-required for timeout/rotation cadence; the concrete missing-verification instance is already covered by the tokens category, avoiding duplicate ownership.

categories.intent: Choice of an RBAC access-control model, adoption of a default-deny authorization posture, and re-verification of authorization on every request rather than trusting a cached decision.
categories.relationshipToSource: Restates the security concern raised under the listed creator.security ledger area(s) as an original classification decision; does not reproduce any ledger item's title or notes text.

exclusion.reason: These are whole-system architecture decisions (which access-control model to adopt, whether the framework's authorization middleware runs on every route) rather than a single detectable code pattern; a repository-local rule cannot certify a system-wide default-deny posture from source patterns alone. Concrete missing-check instances remain covered by the authorization category's four owned rules.

categories.evidenceRequirement: policy-input-required / architecture-decision-required.

categories.intent: Suppressing stack-trace disclosure in production error responses, removing response headers that reveal server/framework identity, disabling directory listing, and turning off insecure default settings shipped by a web framework.

Recorded as a backlog gap rather than force-fit into production-hardening's http-protocol-cache ownership, which covers transport/header/cache/proxy controls that are not framework-default-specific.

categories.evidenceRequirement: policy-input-required / detector-not-yet-built: recorded as a coverage gap, not a false clean claim.
